prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
System: Cedar Falls Municipal Drinking Water Treatment Plant control system. Mission: continuous potable water production meeting regulatory, utility and demand targets; give operators visibility, dependable automatic control and manual intervention points across intake, treatment, laboratory and distribution. Boundary: River Intake Pump Station/Raw Water Screen Channel through treatment, disinfection, finished-water storage to High Service Pump Header. Elements: River Intake Pump Station (alias Ironwood): first pumping within withdrawal limits; normally automatic, pump starts governed by raw-water demand and channel depth. Raw Water Screen Channel: monitored for upstream, downstream and differential level, rake run status, high-debris indications. Coagulant Dosing Skid: chemical feed per setpoints, raw-water conditions, operator direction. North and South Filter Gallery: parallel; provide equipment status, headloss, turbidity, backwash control to staff. Chlorine Contact Basin (disinfection contact); Clearwell Level Controller (finished-water storage); Backwash Recovery Tank; instrumentation; Laboratory Sample Receiving Bench (receives process and compliance samples). SCADA Historian Server (alias Lantern): stores operating data for trends, compliance, incident reconstruction. Req: controllers, local panels, workstations, analyzers and Lantern stay synchronized to plant time. Actors: Chief Operator (overall authority: mode selection, production targets, treatment response, abnormal response; authorizes Storm Intake Mode entry); Duty Engineer (configuration control, control-system problems, approves engineering changes); Maintenance Planner (condition info to planned work, coordinates with operations); Laboratory Technician (analytical confirmation, reports unusual results to operations); Distribution Dispatcher (communicates delivery expectations/demand changes affecting pumping and storage); Chemical Supplier Driver (controlled delivery procedures; inventory changes checked before setpoints affected); Residuals Hauler (residuals/backwash recovery removal); trained staff supervise automatic control, place equipment in safe manual, document deviations. External interfaces: North and South Distribution Pressure Station (influence finished-water pumping; network outside scope), electric power, chemical delivery, lab information, residuals scheduling, distribution communications. Alarm: Chlorine Residual Alarm high-priority (public-health risk, analyzer fault or process condition; immediate operator assessment). Intake modes: automatic normal; Reduced-capacity service (river level, equipment condition or demand limits); Storm Intake Mode (rainfall, river rise, debris, runoff; entered by Chief Operator authorization when normal assumptions unreliable; staff increase observation of river level, screen loading, turbidity, pump cycling).

New part:
S033: A rising differential level across the Raw Water Screen Channel is treated as an early indication of screen blinding or heavy floating debris.
S034: The Raw Water Screen Channel sends the Rake Torque Snapshot at the end of each cleaning cycle to preserve the recorded loading condition.
S035: If the Raw Water Screen Channel shows rapid level change, plant staff verify that the cleaning mechanism is running and that the River Intake Pump Station is not drawing the channel down too quickly.
S036: A high-high level condition at the Raw Water Screen Channel requires immediate field confirmation because it may indicate restricted passage, failed cleaning, or abnormal river backwater.
S037: Raw-water quality triggers include high turbidity, unusual color, odor complaints from field staff, visible sheen, algae accumulation, and rapid temperature change.
S038: When a raw-water quality trigger occurs, the Chief Operator determines whether to adjust pumping rate, request additional laboratory testing, or increase downstream process monitoring.
S039: The Laboratory Technician supports intake decisions by prioritizing raw-water checks when storm runoff or an abnormal visual condition is reported.
S040: The Coagulant Dosing Skid is placed under closer observation when intake turbidity changes faster than the normal control response can stabilize.
S041: The North Filter Gallery and South Filter Gallery are advised when incoming water quality is expected to shorten filter run time or increase solids loading.
S042: Pump permissives at the River Intake Pump Station include adequate suction level, available discharge path, healthy motor status, open isolation valves, and absence of active protective trips.
S043: A pump is not permitted to start when the Raw Water Screen Channel downstream level is below the established low-level limit.
S044: A pump start is also blocked when the associated drive reports a fault, when local control is selected, or when a safety interlock is not proven.
S045: If a permissive is lost during operation, the control system either alarms the condition or stops the affected pump according to the severity of the signal.
S046: The Chief Operator may authorize temporary manual operation only when the cause is understood, the equipment can be observed, and the risk to treatment continuity is acceptable.
S047: The SCADA Historian Server retains river level, screen differential, pump status, and raw-water quality trends for operating review and event reconstruction.
S048: The Duty Engineer reviews storm forecasts and river-stage information when a prolonged debris event or high-flow period is expected.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
